sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访几位商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼等多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Babarro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: The mysterious explosion of a Russian missile has left an entire team of scientists dead.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯一枚导弹的神秘爆炸导致一整个科学家团队丧生。

sentences.en: David Sanger on what that means for an arms race between the United States and Russia that both sides seem to want.
sentences.zh: 大卫·桑格将为您解读这对美俄双方似乎都渴望的军备竞赛意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Friday, August 16th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月16日，星期五。

sentences.en: David, tell me what happened last Thursday in Russia.
sentences.zh: 大卫，请告诉我上周四在俄罗斯发生了什么。

sentences.en: Well, if you were in Moscow, Michael, and you were watching TV, all of a sudden your screen went blue, and there was a big star that appeared on a blue background.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，如果你当时在莫斯科看电视，屏幕会突然变蓝，蓝色的背景上出现一颗大星星。

sentences.en: There was wording up there basically telling people to take cover.
sentences.zh: 上面还有文字，基本上是告诉人们寻找掩体。

sentences.en: It said,
sentences.zh: 上面写着：

sentences.en: A strong wind is expected.
sentences.zh: 预计有强风。

sentences.en: Take cover in a capital building.
sentences.zh: 请在首都建筑内寻找掩体。

sentences.en: Do not shelter or park under trees or rickety structures.
sentences.zh: 不要在树下或摇摇欲坠的建筑物下避雨或停车。

sentences.en: Be careful.
sentences.zh: 请注意安全。

sentences.en: So this is a storm warning.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个风暴预警。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a storm warning, but the oddity is there was no storm.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是风暴预警，但奇怪的是，当时并没有风暴。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, if you were up in northern Russia, up near the White Sea, this is the part of Russia that's sort of closest to Finland,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，如果你在俄罗斯北部，靠近白海的地方，也就是俄罗斯离芬兰最近的那个区域，

sentences.en: and you were looking on the website of one of the local cities, you saw an indication of a big surge, a brief surge in the afternoon in radiation levels.
sentences.zh: 如果你查看当地某个城市的网站，会看到下午辐射水平出现了一次短暂的激增。

sentences.en: This obviously led a lot of people to be concerned, and there were announcements, and there was actually a rush to buy iodine,
sentences.zh: 这显然引起了许多人的担忧，随后出现了相关公告，甚至引发了抢购碘片的浪潮，

sentences.en: because if you remember back to the old Cold War days, people used to stockpile iodine to keep their thyroid from absorbing radiation and causing thyroid cancer.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你还记得冷战时期，人们过去常储备碘片，以防止甲状腺吸收辐射并引发甲状腺癌。

sentences.en: Then, a few hours later, that warning just disappeared from the city website.
sentences.zh: 然后，几个小时后，那个警告就从城市网站上消失了。

sentences.en: So this is sounding kind of mysterious.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实有点神秘。

sentences.en: It's sounding kind of mysterious and really, really ominous.
sentences.zh: 听起来不仅神秘，而且非常、非常不祥。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, there was pressure underway for either local officials or the Russian government to begin to offer some answers about what was going on.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，当地官员或俄罗斯政府面临压力，需要开始对发生的事情给出一些解释。

sentences.en: Now, what everybody knew near this northern Russian town was that there's a big missile test site nearby.
sentences.zh: 现在，这个俄罗斯北部城镇附近的所有人都知道，附近有一个大型导弹试验场。

sentences.en: And the first explanation that the Russians gave was that there had been an accident with a liquid-fueled missile.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯给出的第一个解释是，一枚液体燃料导弹发生了事故。

sentences.en: The problem with that explanation is most liquid-fueled missiles don't produce any radiation.
sentences.zh: 这个解释的问题在于，大多数液体燃料导弹不会产生任何辐射。

sentences.en: So that didn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这说不通。

sentences.en: And then another statement came out that said that actually what happened was an explosion of an isotope power source for a liquid-fueled rocket.
sentences.zh: 接着又发布了另一份声明，称实际上发生的是液体燃料火箭的同位素电源发生了爆炸。

sentences.en: Well, that was the first admission by the Russian government that something involving a radiological event had taken place.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是俄罗斯政府首次承认发生了涉及放射性的事件。

sentences.en: Because isotope suggests radiation.
sentences.zh: 因为同位素意味着辐射。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But of course, the Russians weren't coming clean about exactly what it was.
sentences.zh: 但当然，俄罗斯人并没有完全坦白到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: They didn't say nuclear.
sentences.zh: 他们没有说核。

sentences.en: They didn't say atomic.
sentences.zh: 他们没有说原子。

sentences.en: They didn't say accident.
sentences.zh: 他们没有说事故。

sentences.en: They simply said something went wrong with an isotope power supply.
sentences.zh: 他们只是说同位素电源出了点问题。

sentences.en: And that really got people nervous.
sentences.zh: 这确实让人们感到紧张。

sentences.en: So what actually happened?
sentences.zh: 那么到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, as we tried to piece it together, we got a picture of the Russians testing an entirely new kind of nuclear missile, one that uses a small nuclear reactor to propel it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我们试图拼凑事实时，我们了解到俄罗斯正在测试一种全新的核导弹，它使用小型核反应堆作为动力。

sentences.en: And that in the course of the testing, something went wrong with the nuclear reactor.
sentences.zh: 在测试过程中，核反应堆出了问题。

sentences.en: And over the course of a day or so, we learned that seven people died, that the reactor had actually exploded after it was recovered from the sea,
sentences.zh: 在接下来的一天左右，我们得知有七人死亡，反应堆在从海中打捞上来后发生了爆炸，

sentences.en: and that this had turned into a much larger disaster than the Russians had ever publicly admitted.
sentences.zh: 这演变成了一场比俄罗斯公开承认的规模大得多的灾难。

sentences.en: But David, I thought that Russia and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但是大卫，我以为俄罗斯和美国

sentences.en: don't test nuclear weapons and haven't tested them for years.
sentences.zh: 不测试核武器，而且已经多年没有进行过测试了。

sentences.en: So how do you explain that?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么解释这个？

sentences.en: Well, you're exactly right, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得完全正确，迈克尔。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: and Russia haven't tested any nuclear weapons for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 和俄罗斯已经超过20年没有测试过任何核武器了。

sentences.en: But to understand what's happening here, you have to go back to 2018.
sentences.zh: 但要理解这里发生了什么，你必须回到2018年。

sentences.en: When Vladimir Putin gave his State of the Union address.
sentences.zh: 当时弗拉基米尔·普京发表了国情咨文。

sentences.en: But he did this one with lots of animation.
sentences.zh: 但他这次演讲用了大量的动画演示。

sentences.en: Had a big screen behind him.
sentences.zh: 他身后有一个大屏幕。

sentences.en: And he showed images of three new nuclear delivery systems that Russia was developing.
sentences.zh: 他展示了俄罗斯正在开发的三个新核武器运载系统的图像。

sentences.en: And when you watch the animation, it was incredible and scary and maybe part fantasy.
sentences.zh: 当你观看那些动画时，它既令人难以置信又令人恐惧，甚至可能带有一点幻想色彩。

sentences.en: But here's what he showed.
sentences.zh: 但他展示的是这些。

sentences.en: One of the weapons was an undersea autonomous drone.
sentences.zh: 其中一种武器是水下自主无人机。

sentences.en: Basically, imagine an autonomous torpedo with a nuclear weapon screwed into the nose cone.
sentences.zh: 基本上，想象一枚自主鱼雷，鼻锥上拧着一枚核武器。

sentences.en: And it was quickly dubbed the Poseidon.
sentences.zh: 它很快被称为“波塞冬”。

sentences.en: And the idea was that Russia could have it cruising around in the ocean.
sentences.zh: 其构想是俄罗斯可以让它在海洋中巡航。

sentences.en: And if there was ever a nuclear exchange, and even if Moscow was destroyed and all the nuclear commanders were knocked out or killed,
sentences.zh: 如果发生核交换，即使莫斯科被摧毁，所有核指挥官都被消灭或杀害，

sentences.en: this drone would have built-in instructions to head to the west coast of the United States.
sentences.zh: 这枚无人机也会有内置指令前往美国西海岸。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Undersea, where American missile defenses could never get at it.
sentences.zh: 在水下，美国的导弹防御系统永远无法触及它。

sentences.en: So that was one weapon.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一种武器。

sentences.en: That was the real doomsday machine.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正的末日机器。

sentences.en: The second one was a missile that would move at Mach 5.
sentences.zh: 第二种是一种以5马赫速度移动的导弹。

sentences.en: That's five times the speed of sound.
sentences.zh: 那是音速的五倍。

sentences.en: And would never really manage to go very high up into outer space.
sentences.zh: 而且它永远不会飞得太高进入外太空。

sentences.en: So that the missile itself, again, would avoid missile defenses, which usually are designed to find a predictable arc for an incoming intercontinental ballistic missile
sentences.zh: 这样导弹本身就能避开导弹防御系统，因为这些系统通常旨在寻找洲际弹道导弹的预定轨迹

sentences.en: and destroy it in outer space.
sentences.zh: 并在外太空将其摧毁。

sentences.en: And then the third missile...
sentences.zh: 然后是第三种导弹……

sentences.en: ...was basically a cruise missile, which NATO called Skyfall.
sentences.zh: ……基本上是一种巡航导弹，北约称之为“天陨”。

sentences.en: And a yes, before you ask me, Michael, that is the title of a James Bond movie.
sentences.zh: 是的，迈克尔，在你问我之前，那确实是一部詹姆斯·邦德电影的片名。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 明白吗？

sentences.en: But a cruise missile goes in a zigzag direction.
sentences.zh: 但巡航导弹是呈之字形前进的。

sentences.en: It can reverse itself.
sentences.zh: 它可以掉头。

sentences.en: It can go around mountains.
sentences.zh: 它可以绕过山脉。

sentences.en: It can hug the land.
sentences.zh: 它可以贴地飞行。

sentences.en: And again, it defeats missile defenses because the missile defenses can't even see it.
sentences.zh: 同样，它能击败导弹防御系统，因为防御系统甚至无法发现它。

sentences.en: In fact, radar may not pick up a cruise missile if it's down low enough.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果巡航导弹飞得足够低，雷达可能根本探测不到它。

sentences.en: But what was really strange about this last missile was that it was supposed to be powered by a small nuclear reactor.
sentences.zh: 但这种最后一种导弹真正奇怪的地方在于，它本应由小型核反应堆提供动力。

sentences.en: The nuclear reactor at the back of the missile meant that it could reach any corner of the world.
sentences.zh: 导弹尾部的核反应堆意味着它可以到达世界的任何角落。

sentences.en: Because a nuclear reactor can run for weeks, months, maybe even years.
sentences.zh: 因为核反应堆可以运行数周、数月，甚至数年。

sentences.en: So basically the fuel is limitless and the range of the missile is limitless.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上燃料是无限的，导弹的射程也是无限的。

sentences.en: That's like science fiction.
sentences.zh: 那简直就像科幻小说。

sentences.en: You know what it's like?
sentences.zh: 你知道它像什么吗？

sentences.en: It's like Dr. Strange's look.
sentences.zh: 就像《奇异博士》里的那种样子。

sentences.en: Because the distance is not limited, it can maneuver as long as possible.
sentences.zh: 因为距离不受限制，它可以尽可能长时间地进行机动。

sentences.en: So is that the weapon that we think might have exploded on Thursday night?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们认为周四晚上可能发生爆炸的那种武器吗？

sentences.en: That third kind of weapon that Putin outlined during this speech in 2018?
sentences.zh: 普京在2018年演讲中概述的那第三种武器？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And clearly, David, Vladimir Putin is not trying to hide the fact that Russia is working on these pretty stunning weapons.
sentences.zh: 显然，大卫，弗拉基米尔·普京并没有试图掩盖俄罗斯正在研发这些相当惊人的武器的事实。

sentences.en: I mean, in this speech, he's actively broadcasting to the world that he is working on developing these.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这次演讲中，他正在积极向全世界广播他正在开发这些武器。

sentences.en: Oh, he's not hiding a thing.
sentences.zh: 哦，他什么都没藏着。

sentences.en: I mean, quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It really does show you what the nature of the new arms race is and how it's different from what went before.
sentences.zh: 这确实向你展示了新军备竞赛的本质，以及它与过去有何不同。

sentences.en: Back in the 60s and 70s, the Americans and the Russians would try to hide their developments from each other.
sentences.zh: 回到60年代和70年代，美国人和俄罗斯人会试图向对方隐瞒他们的研发进展。

sentences.en: Eventually, of course, some of them came out.
sentences.zh: 当然，最终其中一些还是会被发现。

sentences.en: But what Putin wanted to do was announce to the public, we're back.
sentences.zh: 但普京想要做的是向公众宣布：我们回来了。

sentences.en: And in fact, remember, he announced this in 2018, just before a major Russian election.
sentences.zh: 事实上，请记住，他在2018年俄罗斯大选前夕宣布了这一点。

sentences.en: And he was basically saying, you know, we are going to restore the power of the old Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，你知道，我们要恢复旧苏联的力量。

sentences.en: You respected the old Soviet Union because it had nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 你们尊重旧苏联，因为它拥有核武器。

sentences.en: And now, having revived the conventional military, Putin was saying,
sentences.zh: 现在，在重振常规军事力量之后，普京在说：

sentences.en: I'm reviving our nuclear force and finding a way to evade all of those anti-missile systems that the Americans have spent $300 billion building over the past 30 years.
sentences.zh: 我正在重振我们的核力量，并找到一种方法来规避美国在过去30年里花费3000亿美元建立的所有反导系统。

sentences.en: So how does the United States react to that disclosure of these new weapons plans by Russia, our longtime adversary?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于我们长期的对手俄罗斯披露这些新武器计划，美国是如何反应的？

sentences.en: Well, the reactions were mixed, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，反应不一，迈克尔。

sentences.en: And there was obviously a group that was pretty freaked out because, you know, not a whole lot has changed in nuclear technology since the fall of the Berlin Wall.
sentences.zh: 显然有一群人感到非常恐慌，因为你知道，自柏林墙倒塌以来，核技术并没有发生太大的变化。

sentences.en: And suddenly here were the Russians announcing a whole new set of weapons.
sentences.zh: 突然间，俄罗斯人宣布了一整套全新的武器。

sentences.en: Then there was a group saying, you know, good luck with that reactor thing.
sentences.zh: 然后有一群人说，祝你们那个反应堆好运吧。

sentences.en: But then there was a third group that was actually pretty gleeful about the entire thing.
sentences.zh: 但还有第三群人，他们实际上对整件事感到相当窃喜。

sentences.en: Gleeful.
sentences.zh: 窃喜。

sentences.en: Gleeful, Michael, because there's a group inside the Pentagon, certainly among many conservatives in the arms world,
sentences.zh: 窃喜，迈克尔，因为五角大楼内部，当然还有军备界许多保守派人士，

sentences.en: who believe the United States has underinvested in its nuclear weapons over the past 10 to 15 years.
sentences.zh: 他们认为美国在过去10到15年里对核武器的投资不足。

sentences.en: And here all of a sudden was the justification for what they've long argued for, which is a renewal of the American nuclear arsenal.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们长期以来所主张的事情——即更新美国核武库——有了正当理由。

sentences.en: So they actually see this, some of them, in the United States as an opportunity to do something that they've wanted to do for a long time, but have felt that they couldn't.
sentences.zh: 所以在美国，他们中的一些人实际上将其视为一个机会，去做一件他们想做很久但一直觉得无法做到的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, Michael, there are two arguments for building up a nuclear arsenal.
sentences.zh: 是的，迈克尔，建立核武库有两个论点。

sentences.en: One is you go to Congress and you say, there's new technology around, we should really do this,
sentences.zh: 一个是你去国会说，现在有了新技术，我们真的应该这样做，

sentences.en: that may not convince very many people and certainly isn't going to convince many of the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这可能说服不了多少人，当然也说服不了多少民主党人。

sentences.en: The other way to go at it is to say, we're falling behind.
sentences.zh: 另一种方式是说，我们正在落后。

sentences.en: And if we don't invest too, we're really going to find that we've got an old system that can't defend against a new class of nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不投资，我们真的会发现我们拥有的旧系统无法防御新一代核武器。

sentences.en: And with Putin's speech, they have what looks like a very legitimate argument that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而随着普京的演讲，他们得到了一个看起来非常合理的论点，即美国

sentences.en: could be falling behind.
sentences.zh: 可能正在落后。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And that's the argument that was working.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个行之有效的论点。

sentences.en: Buried in that more than $700 billion defense budget that President Trump has pushed through is a lot of new money for new nuclear weapons, hypersonic missiles,
sentences.zh: 在特朗普总统推动的超过7000亿美元的国防预算中，隐藏着大量用于研发新核武器、高超音速导弹的资金，

sentences.en: all kinds of weaponry that many in the Pentagon and many defense contractors have been dreaming about for a decade or two.
sentences.zh: 以及五角大楼和许多国防承包商梦想了十到二十年的各种武器。

sentences.en: But now they're getting to go experiment with.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们终于可以去进行试验了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《纽约时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: So at this point, David, you're describing two adversaries who are seeing opportunities to build up their nuclear program.
sentences.zh: 那么大卫，在这一点上，你描述了两个对手，他们都看到了加强各自核计划的机会。

sentences.en: But my sense is that both countries operate under this massive structure of nuclear treaties that mean that neither can do any of the things that you're describing.
sentences.zh: 但我的感觉是，两国都在庞大的核条约框架下运作，这意味着双方都不能做你所描述的任何事情。

sentences.en: So how does that work?
sentences.zh: 那么这是怎么运作的呢？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, the treaties that were signed over the course of decades between Russia and the United States have begun to fritter away.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，俄罗斯和美国几十年来签署的条约已经开始瓦解了。

sentences.en: Some have expired.
sentences.zh: 有些已经过期了。

sentences.en: President Trump, since he came in, made it clear he wanted to get out of at least one, the Intermediate Nuclear Forces Treaty.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统自上任以来就明确表示，他至少想退出其中一项条约，即《中程核力量条约》。

sentences.en: You have to have everybody adhere to it.
sentences.zh: 你必须让所有人都遵守它。

sentences.en: And you have a certain side that almost pretends it doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 而你面对的一方几乎假装它不存在。

sentences.en: Which he said the Russians were violating, and they were.
sentences.zh: 他说俄罗斯人违反了该条约，事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: We can't be put at the disadvantage of going by a treaty, limiting what we do, when somebody else doesn't go by that treaty.
sentences.zh: 当别人不遵守条约时，我们不能让自己处于一种受条约限制、束手束脚的不利境地。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 明白吗？

sentences.en: And that happened just a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 而那件事就发生在几周前。

sentences.en: The United States taking a stand against Russia.
sentences.zh: 美国对俄罗斯采取了强硬立场。

sentences.en: Where the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: ended it.
sentences.zh: 终止了它。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: is pulling out of a decades-long nuclear treaty with Russia, sparking fears of a new arms race we thought was confined to the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 正在退出与俄罗斯一项长达数十年的核条约，这引发了人们对一场我们原以为只局限于冷战时期的军备竞赛的担忧。

sentences.en: And now there's a question about whether the one remaining treaty between the United States and Russia, it's called New Start,
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，美国和俄罗斯之间仅存的一项条约，即《新削减战略武器条约》，

sentences.en: which limits the number of intercontinental nuclear weapons, will even be renewed when it expires in February 2021, just a month after the next presidential inauguration.
sentences.zh: 该条约限制了洲际核武器的数量，它在2021年2月到期时是否还会续签，而那时距离下一任总统就职仅过去一个月。

sentences.en: So this whole structure that's been built up over the past 20 or 30 years to limit both sides and what they can build, that is all crumbling.
sentences.zh: 所以，过去二三十年来建立起来的、旨在限制双方及其武器建造能力的整个结构，现在正分崩离析。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, new technologies are coming up with new kinds of weapons that aren't even covered by the treaties anyway.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，新技术正在催生出各种新型武器，而这些武器甚至根本不在条约的覆盖范围内。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what both Putin and President Trump are experimenting with.
sentences.zh: 而这正是普京和特朗普总统都在尝试的方向。

sentences.en: David, from everything you're saying, both the U.S.
sentences.zh: 大卫，从你所说的一切来看，美国

sentences.en: and Russia are simultaneously casting off this history of denuclearization treaties that limited the size of our arsenals.
sentences.zh: 和俄罗斯正在同时抛弃这段限制我们军火库规模的去核化条约历史。

sentences.en: And we're focused on having less, not more.
sentences.zh: 我们原本专注于减少核武器，而不是增加。

sentences.en: So why are we both seeming to reverse course here?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们双方似乎都在这里反其道而行之呢？

sentences.en: Well, that's exactly right, because the old thing was that these nuclear arms limitation treaties actually created security by reducing the number of nuclear weapons in the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得完全正确，因为过去的老观念是，这些核军控条约实际上通过减少世界上的核武器数量来创造了安全。

sentences.en: The new thing is that these treaties are actually constraining the United States and Russia from adopting new technologies that each one of them wants.
sentences.zh: 而新观念是，这些条约实际上正在限制美国和俄罗斯采用各自想要的新技术。

sentences.en: Putin wants them because he wants to avoid American missile defenses.
sentences.zh: 普京想要这些技术，因为他想避开美国的导弹防御系统。

sentences.en: And he thinks his old weapons won't do that.
sentences.zh: 而且他认为他旧的武器做不到这一点。

sentences.en: Donald Trump wants them because he believes that there are a whole new group of nuclear actors coming in led by China.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普想要这些技术，因为他认为以中国为首的一大批新的核行为体正在涌现。

sentences.en: And he doesn't want to be limited by his old outdated treaties with Russia that prohibit him from building weapons that might counter new competitors.
sentences.zh: 他不想被他与俄罗斯之间那些过时的旧条约所束缚，因为这些条约禁止他制造可能对抗新竞争对手的武器。

sentences.en: So without anyone really announcing it, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，在没有人真正宣布的情况下，美国

sentences.en: has entered a new nuclear arms race, primarily with Russia, but also with China and a host of other growing nuclear powers.
sentences.zh: 已经进入了一场新的核军备竞赛，主要是针对俄罗斯，但也包括中国和其他许多正在崛起的核大国。

sentences.en: That's exactly right, but it's different than the old arms race.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确，但这与旧的军备竞赛不同。

sentences.en: The old arms race was mostly about sheer numbers.
sentences.zh: 旧的军备竞赛主要关乎纯粹的数量。

sentences.en: It was about overwhelming the enemy.
sentences.zh: 它关乎压倒敌人。

sentences.en: The new arms race is all about high technology.
sentences.zh: 而新的军备竞赛完全关乎高科技。

sentences.en: But David, this Russian test on Thursday night over the White Sea, it sounds like a spectacular failure for Putin and for Russia.
sentences.zh: 但是大卫，周四晚上在白海进行的这次俄罗斯测试，听起来对普京和俄罗斯来说是一次惨败。

sentences.en: So what does that mean for the state of the nuclear arms race between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么这对美俄之间的核军备竞赛状态意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: and Russia?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题，迈克尔，因为我们真的不知道。

sentences.en: That's a really good question, Michael, because we really don't know.
sentences.zh: 一种思考方式是，俄罗斯人没有实现他们宏大的梦想，每个人都可以松一口气，我们可以放慢这场军备竞赛的步伐。

sentences.en: In one way to think about it is that the Russians aren't succeeding at their grandiose dreams and everybody can breathe a sigh of relief and we can slow down on this arms race.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我不认为特朗普政府会得出这样的结论。

sentences.en: I don't think that's where the Trump administration is going to come out.
sentences.zh: 我认为你已经开始听到的是，这种公开的尴尬，这次导致科学家死亡并泄露消息的爆炸，

sentences.en: I think that what you're already beginning to hear is this public embarrassment, this explosion that killed the scientists and leaked out,
sentences.zh: 只会促使普京总统投入更多资金。

sentences.en: is only going to drive President Putin to invest more.
sentences.zh: 即使他那核动力导弹的梦想失败了，他也会找到其他方法来制造能够规避美国防御系统并以新方式抵达美国的武器，

sentences.en: And even if his dreams of a nuclear propelled missile fail, he will find other ways to come up with weapons that evade American defenses and that have new ways of reaching the U.S.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了证明他是一个不可小觑的强权。

sentences.en: just to establish that he's a power to be reckoned with.
sentences.zh: 所以如果说有什么影响的话，我认为这次“天陨”事件最终可能会加速双方的军备竞赛。

sentences.en: And so if anything, I think this Skyfall incident could end up speeding up the arms race on both sides.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人会想要证明他们不会被打败，他们会重整旗鼓，制造出更好的东西。

sentences.en: The Russians will want to show that they're not going to be defeated, that they're going to pick themselves up and build something better.
sentences.zh: 而美国人会说，看吧，俄罗斯人正在试验所有这些新技术。

sentences.en: And the Americans are going to say, see, the Russians are experimenting with all this new technology.
sentences.zh: 即使他们没能成功，中国人也会成功的。

sentences.en: Even if they fail at getting there, the Chinese will get there.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最好也加快速度。

sentences.en: So we better speed up too.
sentences.zh: 因此，双方都有真正的动力参与这场军备竞赛，并留在其中。

sentences.en: So both sides have real incentives to be in this arms race, to stay in this arms race.
sentences.zh: 那些看起来像是重大挫折的事情，其实根本算不上挫折。

sentences.en: And what look and feel like major setbacks aren't really setbacks at all.
sentences.zh: 它们只是让每个人都继续投入到军备竞赛中。

sentences.en: They just keep everybody invested in the arms race.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你听听特朗普总统的话，有时如果你听听普京总统的话，

sentences.en: Now, if you listen to President Trump, and sometimes if you listen to President Putin,
sentences.zh: 你会听到的是，你知道，这就是我们需要一种全新的全面军控的原因。

sentences.en: what you hear is, you know, this is a reason that we need a whole new type of comprehensive arms control.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统甚至在过去几周里也说过，我想要涵盖所有核武器的新协议，包括洲际导弹、中程导弹，

sentences.en: And President Trump has said, even in the past few weeks, I want new agreements that encompass all nuclear weapons, intercontinental, intermediate range,
sentences.zh: 这些新技术，我想把它们全部整合在一起。

sentences.en: these new technologies, and I want to wrap it all together.
sentences.zh: 普京在不同时刻也表示过，他可能有兴趣做同样的事情。

sentences.en: And Putin at various moments has indicated he might be interested in doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，特朗普政府已经执政近三年了，他们一次也没有坐下来谈判建立新的军控机制。

sentences.en: But the fact of the matter is, we are nearly three years into the Trump administration, and they have not sat down once over negotiating a new arms control regime.
sentences.zh: 所以很难想象从现在到美国总统大选之间，唐纳德·特朗普会尝试坐下来与弗拉基米尔·普京商定

sentences.en: So it's hard to imagine between now and the American presidential election that Donald Trump is going to try to sit down and work out with Vladimir Putin
sentences.zh: 一项全新的军控协议。

sentences.en: an entirely new arms control agreement.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，考虑到关于特朗普总统与普京之间那种奇怪关系的传闻，我不确定即使他们谈成了一项条约，你是否能让它通过。

sentences.en: And frankly, given what's in the air about the odd relationship between President Trump
sentences.zh: 听起来两国增加核武库的可能性，要比两国坐下来签署核条约的可能性大得多。

sentences.en: and Putin, I'm not sure that you could even get such a treaty through, even if they negotiated one.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑这是否意味着我们将看到更多像俄罗斯北部刚刚发生的导弹爆炸那样的事件。

sentences.en: It sounds like there's a greater likelihood of both countries ramping up nuclear arsenals than there is of both countries sitting down and signing a nuclear treaty.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我认为这完全有可能，核军备竞赛的历史表明，

sentences.en: And I wonder if that means we're going to be seeing more incidents like what just happened in northern Russia with this exploding missile.
sentences.zh: 如果双方不进行对话，那么每一方都会扩充军备，部分原因是为了拥有这些武器，

sentences.en: I think that's entirely possible, Michael, that the history of nuclear arms races is that
sentences.zh: 部分原因是为了在进行谈判时有筹码可以交换。

sentences.en: if both sides aren't talking to each other, then each side builds up in part so that they have them

sentences.en: and in part so they have something to trade away if they do get into a negotiation.
sentences.zh: 当然，在我们担心世界各地核扩散的时刻，朝鲜正在扩充其核武库，

sentences.en: And that may be exactly what's going on here.
sentences.zh: 伊朗也可能在扩充其核武库。

sentences.en: Of course, at a moment when we're seeing nuclear proliferation that we're worrying about around the world, that the North Koreans are building up their nuclear arsenal,
sentences.zh: 让两个最大的核大国——这两个国家拥有的核武器加起来占世界总数的90%以上——建造更多的核武器，这并不是一个很好的榜样。

sentences.en: the Iranians may be building up their nuclear arsenal.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也可能意味着更多的俄罗斯社区突然暴露在辐射峰值中，而政府却试图掩盖这一点。

sentences.en: It doesn't set a really great example to have the two largest nuclear powers, two countries that together have more than 90 percent of all the nuclear weapons in the world,
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，自事故发生以来的这些天，俄罗斯人民感觉如何。

sentences.en: build even more.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，我们也一直在试图弄清楚这一点。

sentences.en: And of course, that could mean more Russian communities suddenly exposed to radiation spikes and government attempts to hide that.
sentences.zh: 当然，俄罗斯人并不急于让西方记者进入这些城镇。

sentences.en: So I wonder how people in Russia are feeling in the days since this accident.
sentences.zh: 但据我们所知，人们感到焦虑、愤怒，并觉得自己被欺骗了。

sentences.en: Well, Michael, we've been trying to figure it out, too.
sentences.zh: 他们有理由感到被欺骗，因为俄罗斯政府至今没有承认这是一次涉及核反应堆且出了问题的导弹测试。

sentences.en: And of course, the Russians aren't exactly eager to let Western reporters into some of these towns.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把所有的小细节摆在那里，但没有把它们拼凑起来。

sentences.en: But from what we can pick up, people are anxious, they're angry, and they feel lied to.

sentences.en: There's a reason they should feel lied to, because the Russian government to this day has not said this was a missile test involving a nuclear reactor that went wrong.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这在某种程度上为那些从过去记忆中想起这些事情的俄罗斯人造成了一种创伤后应激综合征。

sentences.en: They've sort of laid all the little elements out there, but not put it all together.
sentences.zh: 过去曾发生过事故，导弹事故，当然还有核事故，一直到包括

sentences.en: And, you know, this has sort of created a sort of post-traumatic stress syndrome for Russians who remember this from their paSt.

sentences.en: Chernobyl, which was on a far larger scale than what we're seeing in recent days, where the government lied to people and they were exposed.

sentences.en: And of course, many thousands died.

sentences.en: So there is a sort of the old Cold War is back, and so are the anxieties that came with it.

sentences.en: Did the government ever acknowledge what that was?

sentences.en: You know, Michael, we still don't know.

sentences.en: I mean, they said it was a malfunction, but I'm not sure any Russians really believe them,
